text:
If you’re heading out for sunset, you’ve got a dry, partly cloudy finish with the sun slipping away at 6:57, though a north wind will keep it feeling cooler than the 68 on the thermometer. The breeze stays up tonight, especially near the lake, where waves build as high as 2 to 4 feet before easing. Expect a clear-to-partly-cloudy, chilly night with a low around 45.

Saturday looks like the better outdoor day, sunny with a high near 64 and a much lighter north wind. The lake should settle to waves around a foot or less, so the waterfront is in good shape for a daytime outing. Clouds increase Saturday night, with rain becoming possible after 3am. Enjoy the sunset, dress for the breeze, and make Saturday your day for longer plans.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): A blocking high-pressure pattern builds over Quebec and northern New England next week, locking in a stretch of classic late-September weather. Monday features mostly sunny skies, crisp north breezes, and highs near 61°. High pressure reinforces refills of cool, dry air through midweek, keeping daytime highs pleasant in the mid-to-upper 60s (65° Tuesday, 67° Wednesday) alongside full sunshine. Clear skies and light winds will set up chilly overnight lows in the lower 40s to upper 30s each morning, with patchy frost likely in mountain cold spots Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday mornings. The high pressure begins shifting east late week, bringing a minor shower chance (30% chance) Thursday into Friday with highs near 66°.
